name: Kish
overview: Kish is a male individual identified as a Benjamite mentioned in Scripture. He is noted as the father or ancestor of Shimei, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 2:5. This Kish is distinguished from the more prominent Kish known as the father of King Saul, as the text simply refers to him as a Benjamite without linking him to Saul.
namesAndTitles: The name Kish means "bow" or "power," reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. There is no indication that this name was given by God, but it carries connotations of strength or weaponry, which may reflect cultural values.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Kish as the father of Shimei and a descendant of Benjamin, establishing his place within the tribe of Benjamin. Beyond these relationships, no additional family connections are provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Kish's significance lies primarily in his genealogical role within the tribe of Benjamin, contributing to the biblical record of Israelite lineages. His mention helps preserve the heritage and continuity of the Benjamite family lines. Although not linked to King Saul, this Kish's presence in the genealogies underscores the importance of family ancestry in the biblical narrative.
